items.note: Story 1: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose president 1889-1911, creamery 1891.
Story 1: pay by butterfat by test not weight; 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern'.
Section A calls the clause 'the hinge of everything' but never says that payment by fat rather than weight is what made a wrong test cost money.

Teague bookkeeper 1905-1945 and Sill Larrow Green buttermaker are both named with roles in Section A. Effie is named but never called secretary. Credited on the core-fact rule for list items with no REQUIRED line.
Section A gives Selby Vose as manager 1913-1938 but never says he was Gideon's son. The son relation appears only in B3, and B-G credit does not travel into A.
Story 5: an annual station-gain line of 5 1/4% carried to the general account, with the 1898 entry quoted.
Story 1: built winter 1895-96, 7 miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
Story 1: weighed at intake, sampled, 17.6 c.c. pipette charge into a graduated neck, cream hauled down, skim returned.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2: full invoice table, 6 doz. pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
Story 3: 'The true gap was 0.19, the same in every month, February and July alike.' Story 4: constant across seasons.
Never says that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, that there was none in the county, or that the one unverified object defined the answer.
Ansel 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924 (Story 1); dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 8).
The test book is kept by Ansel and begins 4 May 1896, and the bench routine is described. Only the bolded element is gating.
The summary leaf's 1896 average of 3.80 is never given in Section A; the run says only that the 1896 glass was sound. Both figures are required.
Story 4: 8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, about 3.80, back to about 3.61, and the '?' in the book.
Story 1: married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the biggest patron.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why the figures are what they are) is missing from Section A. Both bolded elements are required.
Story 8: died 1934 with the imputation on him; test book to the Historical Rooms in 1959.
Six farms on Hessel Bottom, a wet meadow; Emmet's the largest.
Story 7: weigh book from 1 January 1897, scales always agreed.
Story 3: complaints of low tests from 1902. The two gaps are kept apart: E15 treats 0.17 as the Larrow Green gap and never calls the Hollow-vs-Green gap 0.19.
Story 3: Grigg committee, January-March only, the hay conclusion reported as its finding and then refuted.
Story 7: 200,000 lb on 3.42. Story 2: a proportional error, so richer milk lost more (4.80 read 4.56).
Story 7: to Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, to Hazel 1962.
Jerome Cudd's cheese factory at Alder Corners in Vessey County, 'over the ridge'. 1913 and 1914 are both reported and not reconciled, which is acceptable.
Story 6: from 1915, four of six farmers hauled in the summer flush and went to the station the rest of the year.
'his own new glass and never compared figures with anyone, so his book is independent' plus Vessey County: at least two of the four elements.

Asserts only 8 overlapping seasons (1915-1922) and says the station matched Cudd's in 1924-1930. That contradicts the key's sixteen overlapping seasons (1915-1930), each about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners.
Story 6: the same men's milk tested 3.80 at Cudd's against 3.61 at the station; 'Neither water nor hay can explain that.'
Rosalie, Jerome's daughter ('niece' rejected), took the factory in 1941 and had the figures copied for Ivy in 1958.
Story 2: state inspector Merle Strawn, circuit 1907-1936.
Story 7: 'Strawn's lactometer never found water at the station.'
Story 2: 12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole crate.
Only 'No one, Strawn included, asked what the glass had been doing.' Never says he wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Story 2: ordered 28 June, Ammon reply 2 July, in use July 1923, 1924 average 3.80. Nobody connected it (Story 2/8).
Crate to the loft (Story 2); notebooks sent to the college library in 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume (Story 8).
Story 8: petition January 1925.
Story 8: Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the Ostrey Hollow weigh room.
Story 8: Vose's water, Teague's theft, the 1908 hay report; 'no cause established'.
Story 8: four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook recording the condemnation, which no one laid beside the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 4 May award of $3,800 'without admission', charged to the station account.
One fifth of $19,000 (Story 8), charged to the station account the uncredited fat fed (Story 5).
Ivy (b. 1931), Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland; Vaught named as co-author of Bulletin 471.
Section A lists what she gathered but never says these records had never been in the same room. That idea appears only in G ('No one had laid them side by side').
Story 8: February 1958, crate in the station loft; nine surviving pipettes.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 against 17.6, 0.95; 0.88 short given in Story 2.
Story 2: every test read 95% of true, 3.80 read 3.61, proportional. Story 4: 0.19 is 5 per cent.
Story 5: 40,000,000 lb for 1898-1922, 76,000 lb at 25c = $19,000, and the ledger's credited/received totals give the same 76,000 gain.
Bulletin 471 of October 1958 is present, but the 35/33/24-year intervals are missing. Both bolded elements are required.
Granddaughter, derived Ansel -> Duncan -> Ivy; great-niece rejected.

Second cousins, derived via Roy and Duncan as first cousins. Full vs half siblings is 'left open', and the answer says it doesn't change the degree. That is a lean without a verdict, so it counts as a correct abstention.
Gideon, father; Gideon wrote Article VII, making the station test final, and his son defended it.

Abstention A01 answered with a verdict: 'No relationship is established, and the best evidence says there was none'; E41 'None (S)'. Treats a family denial as outranking the other side instead of declaring the question unsettleable.
76,000; 5.26% of fat credited and 5.00% of fat delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 with line items.
72 pipettes, each 0.88 c.c. short.
26 years 1 month 11 days (accepted equivalent) against 25 full years 1898-1922, with the partial-year reason.
Abstention A02: 'cannot be determined from the sources'; both memories noted.
Variable: the measuring glass, station's own against borrowed, 8 May-10 July.
Tester, patrons, herds, feed, scales, acid, bottles held constant.
Rose to about 3.80, fell back to the old level (3.61) the day the station's glass returned.
Locates the cause in the station apparatus, not milk/men/land; limits: which glass item, how many c.c., the borrowed measure.
Ledger gain (Teague/Kyle/Sill), 1911 interval (test book/Orra/Falke), post-1923 rise (Vose/Falke/Hazel), outside observers.
Independence argued; reasons 1-3 hold without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention A09 at the point of question: the 1916 exchange 'rests on Teague's word alone and cannot be confirmed.' The item is earned, but see the deduction for B3's assertion.
Yes, he knew of the complaint: 1902, the 1908 committee, his 1919 circular.
Manager from 1913 (B3), signed ledger sheets with the gain line, wrote the 1919 water circular: three of five.
Abstention A03: 'cannot be established'. The two office men (Teague, Kyle) answer oppositely; no source records his acknowledgment; signing without reading.
E.g. farms 6 (Q), 1924 average 3.80 (A), weigh book 1897, Orra 1866 (A), crate in the loft (M), Vose manager 1913 (M), circular to nine families.
Near-tie table names both carriers and the breaker for NT-1, NT-11, NT-14, NT-20 and others.
A10 (E3: U, undated, minute book lost) and A06 (E25: U, from outside the lot) are credited. A04 is not declared unsettleable anywhere in B-G.
Self-refutations: r05, r06, r11, r15, r18, r20, r03. Buckets sum to 9; capped at 8.
Pipettes 16.72 against 17.6, 95%; proportional 0.19; onset 1 May 1897 after sound 1896 glass; cessation 12 June 1923 / 3.80 in 1924; nothing on the farms changed.
Watering (Vose, Sill) defeated by the lactometer, the weigh book, Alder Corners.
Theft (Teague, Oram's father) defeated by the ledger surplus, 1911, and the post-1923 rise.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05/0, Jan-Mar sampling, Alder Corners.
Abstention A07 answered '**No.**' The board did not examine the glassware; a verdict sentence, not an abstention.
Abstention A05 answered 'Ansel **suspected the glass**'; E45 'The glass (S, M)'; Frick's account rejected.
Counted at 150 words (hyphenated compounds as one).
Invoice, ledger, weigh book, Alder Corners tests, inspector's notebook, crate/measurement: at least five.
Decoys only 'were blamed'; no wrong headline figures.

deductions.reason: Gullibility A01: asserts no Vose-Keddie kinship (B4 'the best evidence says there was none'; E41 'None').
Gullibility A07: F 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' (also Story 8 'No glassware was examined').
Gullibility A05: F 'Ansel suspected the glass'; E45 resolves the tester's belief as 'The glass'.

Gullibility A09: B3 states in the sheet's own voice that Vose 'told Teague in 1916 to let the station-gain line alone', asserting that the bookkeeper questioned the entries. The deduction follows the sheet even though D2.3 abstains.
